predecessors.text: Cuba, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico and Jamaica, the Caribbean colonies of the Crown of Castile in Cliopatria's last Castile shape (1515)

successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, ceded by the Treaty of Paris (signed 10 December 1898, in force 11 April 1899)

successors.name: Cuban Nationalists
successors.text: Cuba: 'Spain relinquishes sovereignty over Cuba effectively recognizing US occupation'

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: the Carolines, Palau and the Marianas except Guam, sold on 12 February 1899

capitals.name: Itinerant court (Castile), drawn at Valladolid as a placeholder

ledger.x: 1516: the Spanish Empire row opens with the Caribbean colonies, at Charles I's accession (the year Cliopatria starts it).
1519: the Spanish settle Panama.
1521: Tenochtitlan falls to Cortés and the Spaniards.
1524: Santiago de Guatemala founded.
1524: León founded in Nicaragua.
22 April 1529: the Treaty of Zaragoza gives the Moluccas to Portugal.
14 February 1530: the Tarascan king Tangaxuan II is executed and the kingdom passes to the Spanish.

c. 1531: Nuño de Guzmán's expedition founds the kingdom of Nueva Galicia (infobox 'c. 1531'; Queen Joanna named the area 'Reino de Nueva Galicia', undated). The page lists Aguascalientes, Guanajuato, Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Zacatecas as the present-day states; it dates the Mixtón War 1540-1541 and the Audiencia…
1532: Pizarro's Spaniards defeat the Inca at Cajamarca.
1532: Cartagena founded on the Caribbean coast of Colombia.
1534: the Spaniards hold Cuzco and Quito.
1534: Cuzco and Quito pass to Spain.
1535: Lima founded.
1537: Almagro seizes Cuzco and Manco Inca withdraws; the rest of the Inca lands are Spanish.
1538: Bogotá founded in the Muisca highlands.
1541: the Spanish settle Chile.
1546: the northern Yucatán peninsula is conquered.
1550: Concepción founded; Spain advances to the Bío-Bío.
1565: Legazpi settles Cebu.
1565: Menéndez founds St.
1567: Chiloé conquered.
1567: the Neo-Inca State becomes a Spanish vassal.
1571: the Spaniards take Manila.
1571: the vassal status ends (infobox 'Vassal of the Spanish Empire (1567–1571)'); Titu Cusi's reign ends in 1571 (infobox '1563–1571'); war is declared on 14 April 1572.
24 June 1572: the Spanish enter Vilcabamba.
1580: Buenos Aires refounded.
1581: Philip II of Spain becomes king of Portugal and its empire.
1598: Oñate's settlers found New Mexico.
1599: the Mapuche rising wipes out the Spanish south of the Bío-Bío.
1626: the Spanish fortify northern Taiwan.
1640: Portugal rises and leaves the union.
1642: the Dutch take Spanish Formosa.
1655: the English take Jamaica.
1667: the Marianas become a Spanish mission field.
1680: the Pueblo Revolt expels the Spanish from New Mexico.
1692: the Spanish return to New Mexico.
1697: Spain cedes western Hispaniola to France.
1697: the last independent Maya kingdom falls.
1702-1704: Carolina and Creek raiders destroy the northern missions.
14 March 1705: Spain takes Colonia del Sacramento in the War of the Spanish Succession.
1708: Oran falls.
1713: Colonia is returned to Portugal.
1732: Spanish forces under José Carrillo de Albornoz recapture Oran and hold it for the next six decades (Spanish Oran page, no day).
13 January 1750: the Treaty of Madrid fixes the Spanish-Portuguese frontier in South America.
1754: Spain and Portugal send troops to clear the Guaraní from the missions ceded to Portugal in 1750.
1756: the Guaraní are crushed at Caiboaté.
1756: the Misiones Orientales pass to Portugal under the 1750 treaty.
1761: Spain regains the missions.
August 1762: the British take Havana.
1762: the British take Manila.
11 October 1762: Cevallos takes Colonia in the Fantastic War.
1762: France gives Louisiana to Spain in secret.
1763: Havana returns to Spain under the 1763 Treaty of Paris.
1763: Spain holds Rio Grande de São Pedro after the Cevallos expedition.
1763: Spain cedes Florida to Britain.
27 December 1763: Colonia returns to Portugal.
1764: the British hand back Manila.
1767: Charles III expels the Jesuits and the mission state passes under the crown.
1769: Spain occupies Alta California.
February 1776: Portuguese forces advance on the fortified position and the Spanish commander Vértiz is 'forced to withdraw and give up the entire Rio Grande area'.
23 February 1777: Cevallos takes Santa Catarina island as his northern base; 'the garrison fled to the mainland without firing a shot'.
1777: the Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October) gives Spain Colonia and the Misiones Orientales.
1 October 1777: Spain gives the island back in the First Treaty of San Ildefonso: Spain 'acknowledged Portuguese control of Southern Brazil and returned Santa Catarina island'.
11 March 1778: the Treaty of El Pardo gives Annobón and Fernando Pó to Spain.
1779: Spain enters the American war and Gálvez attacks West Florida.
1781: Gálvez completes the conquest of West Florida.
1783: the war ends.
1783: Florida returns to Spain.
1792: Spanish troops leave Oran.
1795: Pinckney's Treaty fixes the border.
18 February 1797: the British take Trinidad.
1801: Portugal retakes the Misiones Orientales.
1801: Toussaint Louverture takes Santo Domingo.
1803: Spain hands Louisiana to France at New Orleans (30 November), three weeks before France passes it to the United States.
1808: the reconquest of Santo Domingo begins.
1809: the French surrender Santo Domingo.
1809: Santo Domingo is Spanish again, for twelve years.
1810: the juntas of New Granada.
1810: the junta of Chile.
1810: Buenos Aires deposes the viceroy.

ledger.x: 1811: Venezuela declares independence.
1811: the Banda Oriental rises.

ledger.x: 1811: Paraguay declares independence.
25 July 1812: the First Republic falls.
6 August 1813: Bolívar's campaign restores the patriot republic.
1814: the royalists retake Chile (the Reconquista).
1814: the Second Republic falls.
1814: Montevideo falls to the United Provinces.

ledger.x: 1814: Montevideo, the last royalist city of the Río de la Plata, is lost (month uncertain: May or June).
ledger.cpn: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

ledger.x: 1815: Morillo's expedition retakes New Granada and Venezuela.
1817: San Martín takes Chile.
1819: Bolívar takes Bogotá.
1821: Carabobo ends Spanish rule in Venezuela.
1821: San Martín enters Lima.
1821: Florida passes to the United States.
1821: Central America declares independence.
1821: New Spain ends.
1821: Santo Domingo proclaims independence.
1822: Pichincha frees Quito.
1824: Ayacucho ends Spanish rule in Peru.
1825: the Veracruz fortress falls (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826'): 'Spanish fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé resisted until 1825-1826'.
1825: the last royalists of Upper Peru surrender.
1826: Callao falls (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826').

1826: Chiloé falls, the last Spanish land on the American mainland-side islands (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826'); 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule.'
1860: Morocco cedes Sidi Ifni.
1861: Spain annexes the Dominican Republic.
1863: the Restoration War begins.
14 April 1864: the Spanish fleet seizes the Chincha Islands.
1865: Spain gives up.
1865: Spain leaves Santo Domingo for good: 'the last Spanish troops departing by July' (infobox 'July 11, 1865').
1866: the Spanish fleet leaves the islands.
1868: the Ten Years' War begins in Cuba.

February 1876: Malcampo's fleet and army take Jolo. the fleet anchored on February 20 and 'The army advanced at daylight on the 29th, the fleet opening upon the forts at the same time' (Spanish-Moro conflict page; the page gives no month for the 29th, February 1876 by the sequence).
1878: the Ten Years' War ends; Cuba stays Spanish.
22 July 1878: the Treaty of Licup.
22 July 1878: Sulu submits to Spain by the Treaty of Licup.
1895: the Second War of Independence begins in Cuba.
August 1896: the revolution begins.

14-15 December 1897: the Pact of Biak-na-Bato ends the first phase ('on December 14 to 15, 1897, the Pact of Biak-na-Bato was signed'); Aguinaldo and the other leaders left for exile in Hong Kong on 24 December 1897.

19 May 1898: Aguinaldo returns and resumes the attacks ('On May 19, Aguinaldo, unofficially allied with the United States, returned to the Philippines and resumed attacks against the Spaniards'); the independence declaration of 12 June 1898 was recognised by neither Spain nor the United States; 'By June 1898, the…
1898: the war ends in the Treaty of Paris.
1898: Spain cedes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines to the United States.
1898: Spain gives up Cuba.
10 December 1898: the Treaty of Paris ends Spanish rule in the Philippines (see the loss to the United States below).
12 February 1899: Spain sells its remaining Pacific islands to Germany.
February 1899: the overseas empire of the Americas, Asia and the Pacific ends; the African posts remain.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Tenochtitlan falls on 13 August 1521 and the Kingdom of New Spain is established on 18 August 1521.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Cuzco and Quito held by 1534, Lima founded 1535; the last Inca stronghold falls in 1572.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Maya
wars.outcome: Spanish victory; the Itza of the Petén are the last, in 1697.

wars.name: Chichimeca War
wars.outcome: Peace made by the crown in 1591; the silver towns of Zacatecas and Guanajuato (founded 1548) are secured.

wars.name: War of the Portuguese Succession
wars.outcome: Philip II recognized as king of Portugal by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581; the Portuguese empire stays under Portuguese administration.

wars.name: Destruction of the Seven Cities (Mapuche uprising)
wars.outcome: The Mapuche reverse colonization south of the Bío-Bío.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Spanish Formosa
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: 'Loss of Spanish Formosa to the Dutch: 26 August 1642'.

wars.name: English conquest of Jamaica
wars.outcome: Jamaica lost to England.

wars.name: Pueblo Revolt
wars.outcome: The Spanish are expelled in 1680 and return in 1692.

wars.name: Carolina and Creek raids on the Spanish missions
wars.outcome: The mission frontier of Georgia and northern Florida is destroyed; St.

wars.name: Guaraní War
wars.outcome: The Guaraní are defeated (Caiboaté, 10 February 1756) and driven from the seven missions ceded to Portugal; the Treaty of El Pardo (1761) annuls the exchange.

wars.name: Seven Years' War (British capture of Manila and Havana)
wars.outcome: Manila (October 1762 to April 1764) and Havana occupied; returned under the 1763 Treaty of Paris, which also cedes Florida to Britain (10 February 1763) while Spain gains Louisiana (23 November 1762).

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1779-1783)
wars.outcome: Spain takes West Florida (Baton Rouge, Natchez, Mobile, Pensacola) and regains East Florida in the Peace of Paris of 1783.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Misiones Orientales
wars.outcome: Portugal takes the Misiones Orientales; confirmed by the Treaty of Badajoz (1801).

wars.name: Reconquista of Santo Domingo
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Palo Hincado (7 November 1808), French capitulation 9 July 1809.

wars.name: Spanish American wars of independence
wars.outcome: Spain loses the mainland by 1825-1826 (Ayacucho 9 December 1824, Callao and Chiloé 1826); 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule.'

wars.name: Dominican Restoration War
wars.outcome: Spain withdraws: annexation annulled in March 1865, last troops gone by July (infobox 'July 11, 1865').

wars.name: Ten Years' War
wars.outcome: Cuba stays Spanish.

wars.name: Cuban War of Independence
wars.outcome: Merges into the Spanish-American War.

wars.name: Spanish-American War
wars.outcome: Protocol of peace 12 August 1898; Treaty of Paris signed 10 December 1898: Spain relinquishes Cuba and cedes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.

wars.name: Fantastic War
wars.outcome: Spanish capture of Colonia del Sacramento (11 October 1762) and Rio Grande de São Pedro; the Treaty of Paris (1763) restores the status quo; Colonia returns on 27 December 1763.

wars.name: Spanish–Portuguese War (1776–1777)
wars.outcome: Portugal retakes Rio Grande in February 1776; Cevallos takes Santa Catarina island (23 February 1777) and Colonia (3 June 1777); the First Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) returns the island and gives Colonia to Spain.

wars.name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1859–1860)
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Tétouan entered 6 February 1860, Treaty of Wad-Ras (26 April 1860) with an indemnity, Spanish administration of Tétouan until it was paid, and the retrocession of Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequeña ('ultimately Ifni').

wars.name: Chincha Islands War
wars.outcome: Spain seizes the Chincha Islands (14 April 1864), shells Valparaíso (31 March 1866), fights the battle of Callao (2 May 1866), then leaves the islands; peace with Peru 1879, Bolivia 1879, Ecuador 1885, Chile 1883, an indefinite armistice in 1871.

wars.name: Spanish–Moro conflict
wars.outcome: Jolo falls to Malcampo's expedition in February 1876; the sultan and his datus submit by the Treaty of Licup (22 July 1878).

wars.name: Philippine Revolution
wars.outcome: The revolution begins in August 1896, pauses with the Pact of Biak-na-Bato (14-15 December 1897), resumes on 19 May 1898 and by June 1898 holds Luzon except Manila and Cavite; Spain cedes the Philippines by the Treaty of Paris.

certainty.note: Claims along the Tordesillas line, mission frontiers and the Amazon are approximate; the Caribbean and Philippine coasts are islands.
Sharper lines: Colonia and the Misiones Orientales (San Ildefonso 1777, undone 1801), the 31st parallel (Pinckney 1795) and the Adams-Onís line (1819); the interior of South America stays soft.

The coasts of the island colonies (Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam) are sharp, but the Philippines are soft: the Spanish East Indies page says the highlands of Luzon stayed outside Spanish control until the early 19th century, Mindanao was…
The Pacific islands sold by treaty on 12 February 1899 and the African posts, whose coasts are the shapes.
